exclusions_not_holding.part: RP2354B (PIO, the fixed input's own decoder)
exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: count rate: with pico-examples' quadrature_encoder program, whose worst-case loop is 10 cycles ('able to read step rates up to sysclk / 10'), one state machine reads 15 Msteps/s at the RP2350's 150 MHz clk_sys, under 20 Mcounts/s
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: The figure is the limit of one published program on one state machine, not of the RP2354B's PIO. The RP2350 datasheet (build-date 2025-07-29, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf, read 2026-09-29T03:31:08Z) states the needed facts. Section 11.2.2: 'Each instruction takes precisely one cycle, unless it explicitly stalls (such as the WAIT instruction)'. Section 11.4.2: JMP conditions include 'X--: scratch X non-zero, prior to decrement' and 'Y--', and JMP PIN branches on the GPIO selected by EXECCTRL_JMP_PIN. Each GPIO input has a 2-flipflop synchroniser, which adds the same fixed delay to A and B. clk_sys is 150 MHz. P2 did not evaluate a split across two state machines, one per channel. Each would WAIT for its channel's rising and then falling edge, take JMP PIN on the other channel, and count forward edges with JMP X-- and reverse edges with JMP Y--. That is 3 instructions per edge. At 5 MHz a channel gives 10 M edges/s, 15 clk_sys cycles per edge, and the other channel's edges fall 50 ns (7.5 cycles) away. The loop itself therefore fits the 20 Mcounts/s with margin, taking 2 state machines and roughly 6 to 8 instruction words each. Not established: no such program is written or tested. The read-out of X and Y (an exec'd MOV/PUSH or an in-loop push) and its cost to the loop are not worked out. The index capture's state machine or timer is not counted. The re-rank or P5 has to settle the count before the RP2354B is ruled in or out, so the drop does not hold as stated
